goal: Back off repeated provider HTTP 401 retries for retained operation/lifecycle work, and immediately rearm those retries when a validated replacement credential is saved.
context: Production 2daa37f is healthy with scoped TLS savings verified. Read-only failure ledger shows Vultr operation/lifecycle items hitting HTTP401 every64seconds for 800-1260 attempts, with no possibility of progress until credential repair. Preserve all operations, unknown outcomes, provider-confirmed receipts, checkpoint ownership, mutation proofs, cleanup eligibility and error-driven state transitions. Only when per-account economy is enabled AND kind is operation/lifecycle AND a typed providers.Error has Class ErrorAuthentication and StatusCode401, store a fixed safe PROVIDER_AUTH_RETRY marker and use a five-minute retry delay in the existing atomic failure ledger. Existing RetryDelay hints take precedence; transient/network/proxy-auth407/untyped errors and flag-off retain existing exponential behavior. No skip based on stale account state. On successful validated token replacement, transactionally set next_retry_at=now() only for same-account operation/lifecycle rows carrying the exact marker; retain counters, records, checkpoints and operation state. Failed credential validation/transaction must not rearm. Add isolated-PostgreSQL concurrency/rollback/flag/canary/error-class tests and API-path credential rearm regression. Expand race gate to worker in addition to previous six packages. Full suite plus actual exact-source API review. No subagents. Do not touch the running production version until current 15-minute sample finishes. During that sample two new DigitalOcean accounts were added externally (now10 vs baseline8), so report cohort/workload differences honestly and never claim 90% based on incomparable totals. Canary with existing rollout; no production fault injection or replacement of user credentials. Standard coordinated upgrade and obsolete-browser retirement only. Concurrency detail: take an account row SHARE lock before reading current secret.updated_at and native checkpoint.created_at in a separate READ COMMITTED statement. No checkpoint means no long auth backoff. If the credential changed at/after the attempt start, retry in two seconds instead of five minutes. Replacement takes same account row UPDATE lock before exact-marker rearm; both commit orders are tested. Existing native checkpoint complete transaction owns the checkpoint row throughout; new code only reads it.
commit_message: perf(worker): pace rejected credential retries and rearm on repair
